files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller checklist

Owner: R. Halloway. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July; some months all runs pay in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to prevent a duplicate posting. If the amortization is missing, book it as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after first verifying what is already recorded in the GL.
5. Check June vendor-bill documents against the GL to verify expense coding. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Halcyon Grid Software began in 2019 when a utility-operations analyst and a software engineer compared notes after yet another planning meeting run through spreadsheets, email threads, and marked-up screenshots. They believed smaller energy teams deserved the same operational visibility as large enterprises without having to deploy a sprawling consulting project.

The company now sells a hosted workflow platform for teams that coordinate grid maintenance, field requests, capacity planning, and internal approvals. Customers use configurable work queues, audit trails, dashboards, and integrations to keep operational information in one place. The product is designed to sit alongside existing utility and engineering systems rather than replace them.

The team is compact and practical. Engineers regularly join customer calls, the support lead maintains an unusually detailed library of implementation notes, and sales conversations tend to include live product walk-throughs rather than polished theater. Remote work is common, though the group still gathers for planning sessions and product reviews.

Halcyon Grid Software is currently focused on dependable service, careful product improvements, and stronger onboarding for growing customer teams. Leadership is also refining partner marketing and internal operating routines so the business can scale without losing the direct, helpful style that shaped its early customer relationships.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Position Halcyon Grid Software as the practical operations layer for grid teams that have outgrown spreadsheets but do not want a heavy transformation program. Keep the voice informed, direct, and grounded in day-to-day customer work.

## Q3 priorities

- Refresh core messaging around workflow visibility, auditability, and faster handoffs.
- Update the website's product pages with clearer use cases and shorter demonstrations.
- Run two educational webinars featuring product specialists and customer-facing staff.
- Build a reusable field guide from common implementation questions.
- Recruit a small group of integration and advisory partners for a co-marketing pilot.

## Q4 priorities

- Publish customer stories focused on operational outcomes and adoption lessons.
- Run two additional webinars, using Q3 attendance questions to shape the topics.
- Test partner-led roundtables for utility operations and engineering audiences.
- Equip sales with refreshed overview slides, demo narratives, and follow-up material.
- Review channel quality and document recommendations for the next planning cycle.

## Measures

Track qualified conversations, webinar engagement, content-assisted opportunities, partner participation, and movement from first meeting to product evaluation. Favor signals of genuine buying interest over raw traffic.

## Open items

Confirm campaign ownership, finalize the editorial calendar, select pilot partners, and align available spend after the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# A few handoff notes

R. Halloway — a few things I learned the hard way:

- The bank's own service fees and charges usually appear near the end of the statement. They have historically been booked during close, so do not assume the ledger already has them.
- I was moving quickly in June, and the expense coding on one or two vendor bills may be wrong. Treat the source documents in `bills/` as authoritative and reclass the GL where needed.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. The one-off items that arrived in June were never part of the plan, and they are the reason the larger variances show up.
- Payroll timing is different this time: the second June run pays in early July. Check the payroll register and handle the accrual from there.
